headline: Oil jumps 3% after Trump says U.S. needs no deal with Iran
summary: The stories that stayed in the briefing most this week: Oil jumps 3% after Trump says U.S. needs no deal with Iran; Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat as Hyde-Smith concedes; Immigration minister hits back after Poilievre calls budget plan 'bonkers'.

top.headline: Oil jumps 3% after Trump says U.S. needs no deal with Iran
top.what: Brent crude settled near US$96 a barrel on Thursday after President Trump wrote that the United States no longer needs an agreement with Iran and took Vice-President JD Vance off the talks. Iran's military said four tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat as Hyde-Smith concedes
top.what: News organizations projected Democrat Scott Colom the winner over Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday, eight days after the vote, and she phoned him to concede.
top.why: In the briefing on 6 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Immigration minister hits back after Poilievre calls budget plan 'bonkers'
top.what: Immigration Minister Lena Diab on Thursday defended the immigration measures in last week's federal budget as temporary and aimed at people already in Canada, after Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre attacked the plan in a video.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Ontario plans OSAP caps and online-program ban for private career colleges
top.what: Colleges Minister Nolan Quinn on Thursday outlined legislation that would limit how fast OSAP-funded enrolment can grow at private career colleges and cut off student aid for programs taught mainly online. The bill is expected to be tabled Monday.
top.why: In the briefing on 5 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada's U.S. envoy warns tariffs are raising costs and chilling investment
top.what: Ambassador Mark Wiseman said tariff uncertainty is pushing up costs and discouraging business expansion, a day after Carney said the Trump administration remains Canada's main negotiating partner.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Toronto freezes most hiring as it faces a $1.1-billion budget gap
top.what: With Premier Ford ruling out a second 'New Deal', Toronto has paused most hiring to start closing a projected $1.1-billion shortfall in its 2027 budget.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Absent Democrats let Hegseth impeachment die; House GOP picks Jim Jordan as leader
top.what: Eleven Democrats missed Tuesday's 211-204 vote that shelved impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, enough to have changed the result, and House Republicans chose Jim Jordan to lead them in the minority.
top.why: In the briefing on 4 of the last 7 days.

top.headline: Canada-U.S. trade talks continue as Democrats vow to repeal tariffs
top.what: Tariffs on Canadian goods remain while talks continue, and the DNC chair says Democrats would move to end them if they win power.
top.why: In the briefing on 3 of the last 7 days.
